items.followUp: Define an element and describe metals, non-metals and metalloids, giving an example of each.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature that an element contains only one kind of atom.
rubric.description: An element is a pure substance made up of only one kind of atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Checks identification of metals and a suitable example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming metals and giving a suitable example.

rubric.why: Checks identification of non-metals and a suitable example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming non-metals and giving a suitable example.

rubric.why: Checks identification of metalloids and a suitable example.
rubric.description: Metalloids have some properties of metals and some of non-metals; examples include silicon and boron.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming metalloids and giving a suitable example.

modelAnswer: An element is a pure substance made up of only one kind of atom.
Elements are classified into three kinds:
1. Metals generally conduct heat and electricity; examples include iron and copper.
2. Non-metals are generally poor conductors; examples include oxygen and sulfur.
3. Metalloids have some properties of metals and some of non-metals; an example is silicon.

items.followUp: Define a co-ordinate covalent bond and explain how it forms in the hydronium ion, H3O+.

rubric.why: Checks that a co-ordinate covalent bond involves a shared pair of electrons.
rubric.description: It is a type of covalent bond involving a shared pair of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the covalent bond and shared pair.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature that one atom supplies both bonding electrons.
rubric.description: Both electrons in the shared pair are donated by the same atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one atom donates both electrons.

rubric.why: Checks the electron-pair donor in the example.
rubric.description: In NH3, nitrogen has a lone pair of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the nitrogen lone pair in NH3 as the donor.

rubric.why: Checks the donation of the lone pair to H+ and the resulting ammonium ion.
rubric.description: NH3 donates its lone pair to H+ to form NH4+.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing the correct donation and product.

rubric.why: Checks that the bond formed by the donated pair in the example is identified as co-ordinate.
rubric.description: The donated pair forms a co-ordinate covalent bond in NH4+.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the resulting bond as co-ordinate covalent.

modelAnswer: A co-ordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond in which both electrons of the shared pair are donated by the same atom.
For example, nitrogen in NH3 has a lone pair of electrons.
Nitrogen donates this lone pair to H+: NH3 + H+ → NH4+.
The donated pair forms a co-ordinate covalent bond in NH4+.
